name: Dallas
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Dallas, TX 2026
seo_description: Dallas Christmas events for kids 2026: Dallas Holiday Parade, Trains at NorthPark, Candlelight at Dallas Heritage Village, Zoo Lights and the Arboretum.
lede: The story of Christmas in Dallas runs through Candlelight at Old City Park, held for more than fifty years in the city's first public park, and the Dallas Holiday Parade, which first marched downtown on December 3, 1988. Since then families have added the Trains at NorthPark, the giant tree at Galleria Dallas and, since 2014, the 12 Days of Christmas gazebos at the Dallas Arboretum.
sections: Candlelight in Dallas' oldest park, a tradition for more than fifty years

City Park opened in 1876 as Dallas' first public park, according to the Old City Park Conservancy. Decades later, the Dallas County Heritage Society moved a threatened plantation house into the park, the first of 21 historic buildings that turned it into a living history village. Candlelight grew up there. Katy Trail Weekly marked the 50th Candlelight in 2022 and called it the longest operating holiday event in Texas, held among the state's largest collection of 19th century pioneer and Victorian buildings. Today City of Dallas Park and Recreation runs it as Holiday Village: Featuring Candlelight, with Santa at the Law Office, a petting zoo, carolers and a Polar Express Train ride.
A parade, a giant tree and twelve gazebos

The Dallas Holiday Parade began on December 3, 1988, when employees of The Adolphus hotel and Children's Medical Center Dallas produced it for a crowd of 70,000, the parade says. At Galleria Dallas, FOX 4 reports, crews build a 95 foot tree in the middle of the ice rink, with more than 215,000 lights and 15,000 ornaments, billed as the nation's tallest indoor Christmas tree. The Dallas Arboretum opened its 12 Days of Christmas gazebos in 2014 and planned them for five years. Families kept coming, and the Arboretum says 2026 is the last season to see them.
Trains at Christmas: NorthPark, the M-Line and Union Station

The Trains at NorthPark, which benefits Ronald McDonald House of Dallas, sends hundreds of toy trains along 1,600 feet of track on a journey across America; its 2016 fact sheet called that year its 29th. Downtown, the McKinney Avenue Transit Authority was founded in 1983 by Phil Cobb and Ed Landrum after they found old streetcar tracks paved over on McKinney Avenue. Its trolley opened on July 22, 1989, on a 2.8 mile route and now carries over 400,000 riders a year. Eddie Bernice Johnson Union Station links DART Red and Blue Line light rail, the Trinity Railway Express and Amtrak's Texas Eagle.
celebrates: Dallas celebrates with a mix of history, big displays and trains. The season brings Candlelight to Old City Park, the Dallas Holiday Parade downtown, the 95 foot indoor tree and skating rink at Galleria Dallas, and the Trains at NorthPark for Ronald McDonald House. The Dallas Arboretum fills its garden with the 12 Days of Christmas gazebos for one final year in 2026. Museums join in, from Santa arriving by helicopter at the Frontiers of Flight Museum to gingerbread building at the Perot Museum, and neighborhoods such as Lakewood light their own trees.
lastyear: In 2025 the Dallas Holiday Parade was planned for Saturday, December 6, through downtown, CBS News Texas reported. PaperCity Magazine reported that the Trains at NorthPark returned for the 2025 season in a new space with the same mission of raising money for Ronald McDonald House of Dallas. FOX 4 covered crews building the 95 foot tree at Galleria Dallas, decorated with more than 215,000 lights and 15,000 ornaments and set in the center of the skating rink.
facts: Candlelight is older than most Dallas families' memories: Katy Trail Weekly counted its 50th celebration in 2022. The first Dallas Holiday Parade in 1988 drew 70,000 people. The Arboretum's 12 Days of Christmas gazebos were designed for a five year run starting in 2014 and lasted twelve seasons. The M-Line Trolley came about because two residents spotted forgotten streetcar tracks under the pavement of McKinney Avenue.
trains: Dallas is an easy place to make a train day of Christmas. DART Red and Blue Line light rail, the Trinity Railway Express to Fort Worth and Amtrak's Texas Eagle all stop at Eddie Bernice Johnson Union Station downtown. The M-Line Trolley runs vintage streetcars through Uptown and connects with DART at CityPlace/Uptown Station. The Trains at NorthPark has hundreds of toy trains on 1,600 feet of track, and the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco are a short drive north.

kidfact: The Christmas tree inside Galleria Dallas is 95 feet tall, stands right in the middle of an ice skating rink and wears about 15,000 ornaments, FOX 4 reports.
faq: What is the oldest Christmas tradition in Dallas?

Candlelight at Old City Park is one of the oldest. Katy Trail Weekly marked its 50th celebration in 2022 and called it the longest operating holiday event in Texas. It takes place in City Park, which opened in 1876 as Dallas' first public park, among historic homes, a church and a schoolhouse moved there by the Dallas County Heritage Society.
When did the Dallas Holiday Parade start?

The first Dallas Holiday Parade was held on December 3, 1988. Employees of The Adolphus hotel and Children's Medical Center Dallas produced it to mark the 75th anniversaries of both, WFAA reports, and the parade says a crowd of 70,000 came to watch. It still travels through downtown Dallas each December.
Is the 12 Days of Christmas exhibit at the Dallas Arboretum ending?

Yes. The Dallas Arboretum told FOX 4 that the 12 Days of Christmas gazebos will retire after the 2026 holiday season. The glass sided gazebos first appeared in 2014 and were designed for a five year run, but families kept returning, so they stayed for twelve seasons. This winter is the last chance to see them.
Where can kids see trains at Christmas in Dallas?

The Trains at NorthPark has hundreds of toy trains on 1,600 feet of track and benefits Ronald McDonald House of Dallas. The M-Line Trolley runs vintage streetcars in Uptown, and Union Station downtown serves DART light rail, the Trinity Railway Express and Amtrak. Holiday Village at Old City Park includes a Polar Express Train ride with admission.
How tall is the Galleria Dallas Christmas tree?

FOX 4 reports the Galleria Dallas tree is 95 feet tall, with more than 215,000 lights and 15,000 ornaments, and calls it the nation's tallest indoor Christmas tree. Crews build it in the center of the mall's ice skating rink, so families can skate around it during the holiday season.
